title: Microburst congestion quant kernel investigation - Sept 2025
content:
Purpose and quick TL;DR:

This note captures an exploratory investigation into short-duration client-side microbursts that trigger kernel-level congestion under several quantization modes (INT8, FP8, GPTQ, AWQ). Goal is to surface a reproducible bench, initial root causes, and tactical mitigations we can pilot in the runtime scheduler and kernel selection layer.

TL;DR summary:
- Reproducible microburst pattern (200–500 requests/sec sustained for 2–6s) created consistent 95/99th tail latency spikes and occasional top-1 quality regressions for AWQ/GPTQ variants on our V100/RTX8000-like fleets.
- Primary bottleneck appears to be kernel queueing + L2-bandwidth bursts on multiplexed lanes rather than pure compute saturation.
- INT8 tends to have higher throughput but more sensitivity to scheduler-induced fragmentation; AWQ & GPTQ show sporadic cache-thrashing that correlates to quality regression windows.
- Short-term mitigations: burst admission caps, priority bucketing for long-context sessions, opportunistic fallback to robust kernel variants during burst windows.

Background/context:
- This started from several customer incidents (JIRA SRV-987) where production apps observed elevated hallucination rates and tail latency during traffic spikes. Customer reported use-cases with many short lived chat messages (bot bursts).
- We suspect interplay between: quant kernels with differing memory-access patterns, our dispatcher occupancy algorithm, and KV cache prefetch behavior.
- Notebook-runner: bench harness lives in GH:repo/serving-runtime#4123; small scripts under perf/bench/microburst.

Bench setup (how to reproduce locally):
- Hardware: single 80GB A100 / 40GB A100 / V100 cluster node (tests done across 3 instance types).
- Model: open-gpt-xxl-slim (32k context) compiled to each quant profile: FP16 baseline, INT8-GPTQ, AWQ-8, FP8-mixed.
- Kernel builds: stock cuda kernels and our optimized tiled kernels (tag: kernel-mux-v2).
- Traffic generator: goreq-burst (python harness) sending exponential-arrival bursts:
  - pattern A: baseline steady 50rps 
  - pattern B (microburst): 300rps for 3s, back to 50rps for 7s, repeat x30
- Payload: short prompts (avg 40 tokens), sometimes with long-history (2k tokens) to exercise KV cache.
- Measurements captured: per-request latency (p50/p95/p99), token compute-time breakdown, L2/SM throughput (NVIDIA CUPTI), kernel queue length, KV cache hit rate, and output-quality score vs golden references (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-dist).

Key observations (detailed):
1) Latency tail correlates with kernel queue spikes, not GPU SM utilization
   - During bursts SM utilization hovered 60–80% but kernel queues (dispatch queue length) spiked and then drained causing 150–400ms p99 jumps.
   - Suggests queuing contention when many short requests interleave across GPU resources.

2) Bandwidth micro-thrashing for AWQ/GPTQ variants
   - AWQ shows higher L2 read amplification for small-batch KV lookups; CUPTI traces show bursts of L2 traffic coincident with quality regressions (embedding divergence increases).
   - Hypothesis: quantized weight decompression / reblocking causes transient cache eviction patterns that impact next requests' activations, increasing numerical noise.

3) INT8 kernels are throughput-friendly but fragmentation-sensitive
   - When dispatcher assigns many tiny batches, packed INT8 kernel expects amortized token counts; fragmentation leads to poor SIMD lane utilization and increased per-token overhead.

4) FP8 mixed execution was more robust to quality drift but at higher average token cost
   - FP8 runs had smaller variance in output metrics across bursts; cost/latency trade still unfavorable for price-sensitive customers.

Representative numbers (A100, short prompt, pattern B):
- FP16 baseline: p50 42ms, p95 98ms, p99 165ms
- INT8-GPTQ: p50 28ms, p95 120ms, p99 360ms (queue spikes)
- AWQ-8: p50 24ms, p95 140ms, p99 520ms (L2 thrash + occasional quality delta >0.06 embedding-dist)
- FP8-mixed: p50 32ms, p95 105ms, p99 190ms

Quality signals observed:
- Measured embedding cosine distance vs golden responses for 1k sampled prompts. AWQ showed clusters of higher distance aligned to kernel-thrashing windows. GPTQ had sporadic token-level substitutions for rare tokens during high queue-pressure periods.

Repro strategy notes (to help triage):
- Run microburst harness with --seed=42 and enable CUPTI traces for 30s around a burst window. Collect kernel timelines (driver timestamps) + kernel-name + lane-id mapping.
- Use perf/annotate/kv-prefetch-log to surface whether KV prefetch scheduled out-of-band is colliding with weight decompress calls.

Short-term mitigation proposals (order by implementation effort):
1) Admission control: cap burst admission per GPU to X requests/sec and queue remainder at proxy level (cheap, immediate).
2) Prefer robust kernel variants during detected burst windows: switch AWQ->FP8-kernel when queue depth crosses threshold (requires safe fallback plumbing; medium effort).
3) Adjust dispatcher batching policy: coalesce into slightly larger batches for INT8 to improve lane packing (risk: increases average p50 slightly; low-medium effort).
4) KV prefetch throttling: delay background prefetches when kernel queue is high (medium effort).
5) Lightweight priority buckets: mark long-context sessions higher priority so their KV/cache locality preserved; short bursts get lower priority.

Open questions / things to validate:
- Is the observed L2 thrashing unique to AWQ weight layout, or is it a function of our block-reordering logic? (compare AWQ-raw vs AWQ-reordered builds)
- Can we design a micro-benchmark that isolates weight-decompression L2 footprint from KV access footprint?
- Are there kernel fusion opportunities (decompress + matmul) to reduce transient traffic spikes?
- What is the customer impact threshold where we prefer FP8 fallback vs slight cost increase? (get product guidance)

Immediate next steps (who-does-what):
- Jamal: implement admission cap prototype in dispatcher and run 24h soak with customer workload trace (due 2025-09-16).
- Priya: instrument weight-decompress trace points + add AWQ raw/reordered comparative run (due 2025-09-12).
- Luca: try opportunistic kernel-switch prototype (runtime flag) and measure switch latency/regression surface (due 2025-09-20).
- Maya (owner): compile experiment report and decide canary plan for dispatcher cap (due 2025-09-21).

Notes to self / scratchpad:
- saw odd stderr lines from cuda-driver about l2-eviction-pressure at 2025-09-04 03:12; capture more driver logs next run.
- maybe add a synthetic test that flips quantized kernel block-order to reproduce thrash deterministically.

References and related artifacts:
- GH perf harness: GH:repo/serving-runtime#4123 (microburst harness)
- Past related notes: kernel-jam-quant-chaos-scan-apr2025.json (helpful for strategy but this doc focuses on short microbursts)
- Customer incident: JIRA SRV-987

Appendix: quick commands / snippets
- run harness: python perf/bench/microburst/run.py --pattern B --duration 300 --model open-gpt-xxl-slim --quant AWQ-8 --kernels kernel-mux-v2 --cuptraces out/cuptraces
- capture kernel timeline: python tools/trace_extractor.py out/cuptraces --window 30 --burst-index 4 > traces/burst4.timeline
- quick analysis: scripts/plot_tail_vs_queue.py traces/burst4.timeline --out html/burst4.html

End of note.

(If this turns into a playbook we should move cleaned steps + metrics thresholds to confluence and create an ops runbook for on-call).
